title: With parseNestedJsonStrings on, an identical value keeps or loses its type depending on its LENGTH
rationale: parseNestedJsonStrings(true) deliberately converts JSON-bearing strings into structure - that is the opt-in. The bug is that maxJsonStringLength gates it, so two strings of the same kind differing only in size come out as different TYPES. A performance guard has been given semantic authority.
catchesBugClass: Fidelity that depends on payload size rather than payload type. Also catches any change to the gate boundary condition that would move which values are affected.
cannotCatch: Uses an artificially low limit, so it proves nothing about behaviour at the shipped default of 1,000,000. It also does not cover a string that is valid JSON only after the unescapeJson fallback pass.

predicted.detail: shortJson is expanded into structure; longJson is kept verbatim. Neither field round-trips to its input, and they fail in opposite directions from the same authored type.
